nf763882800b.s: Separation of the judiciary from the executive is directed by which Article?
nf763882800b.x: Article 50 directs separation of the judiciary from the executive; international peace and security is Article 51.

n989c71f64ed.s: The classification of Directive Principles into Socialist, Gandhian and Liberal-intellectual groups is:
o: An academic arrangement used for study
Made by the Supreme Court in Part IV
n989c71f64ed.x: The Constitution does not itself classify the Directive Principles; the three-fold grouping is an academic arrangement.

nindian-polity-20-10.s: How many Articles make up the Liberal-intellectual group of Directive Principles?
nindian-polity-20-10.x: The Liberal-intellectual group has seven Articles, including 44 (UCC), 45, 48 and 48A.

nindian-polity-19-14.s: The prohibition of the slaughter of cows and calves is a directive under Article:
nindian-polity-19-14.x: The cow-slaughter ban is in Article 48; Article 46 promotes the interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections.

nbe698119cd3.s: After the constitutional changes relating to education, Article 45 directs the State to provide:
o: Free legal aid to all citizens
Early childhood care and education until six years of age
Free and compulsory education from six to fourteen years
nbe698119cd3.x: Article 45 now covers early childhood care and education until six; education from six to fourteen is the Fundamental Right under Article 21A.

nindian-society-9-8.s: Which clause of Article 39 concerns the development of children?
nindian-society-9-8.x: Article 39(f) concerns the development of children; Article 44 is the Uniform Civil Code and nutrition is Article 47.

n7f33ebdebfe.s: Directive Principles generally impose which kind of obligation on the State?
o: Positive obligations requiring the State to act
n7f33ebdebfe.x: Directive Principles generally require the State to undertake welfare measures, while Fundamental Rights mostly restrain the State.

n455b0c66d3a.s: Article 40 (organisation of village panchayats) was implemented through the:
n455b0c66d3a.x: Article 40 was given effect by the 73rd Amendment, 1992; the RTE Act implements Articles 45/21A.

nea291441b0b.s: Who described the Directive Principles as 'a veritable dustbin of sentiments'?
nea291441b0b.x: 'Dustbin of sentiments' was T.T. Krishnamachari's phrase; Granville Austin called FRs and DPSPs the conscience of the Constitution.

n67de70b070f.s: The non-enforceability of the Directive Principles in courts arises from:
o: The ideal of international peace in Article 51
The aim of a welfare state in Article 38
n67de70b070f.x: Non-enforceability arises from the express bar in Article 37, not merely from their role as a guide to law-making.

nc1a705967a7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the use of Directive Principles in interpretation?
o: Article 48A read with Article 21 supports the right to a healthy environment
Non-justiciability excludes Directive Principles from constitutional interpretation
Article 45 read with Article 21 has been used to enrich Fundamental Rights
Courts use Directive Principles to enrich Fundamental Rights
nc1a705967a7.x: Non-justiciability does not exclude Directive Principles from interpretation; courts read them with Fundamental Rights, e.g. Article 48A with 21.

n49b914ba570.s: Which case adopted the doctrine of harmonious construction between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles?
o: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951)
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950)
n49b914ba570.x: Harmonious construction came in In re Kerala Education Bill (1958); Champakam (1951) held that Fundamental Rights prevail.

nfd4383db760.s: Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule were inserted by the:
nfd4383db760.x: The First Amendment, 1951 created Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule to shield land-reform laws; the Schedule later grew to over 280 entries.

n9df29800fca.s: In Kesavananda Bharati, which part of Article 31C was struck down?
o: The first part protecting laws for Articles 39(b) and 39(c)
The second part excluding judicial review
n9df29800fca.x: Kesavananda Bharati upheld the first part of Article 31C but struck down the second part, which excluded judicial review.

n47b507788c4.s: In Property Owners Association v. State of Maharashtra, whether a privately owned resource falls under Article 39(b) depends on:
o: Its ownership by the Union Government alone
Nothing, since every private resource is automatically covered
Its nature, scarcity, effect on community well-being and concentration in private hands
Nothing, since no private resource can ever be covered
n47b507788c4.x: The Court held private ownership alone does not bring a resource within Article 39(b); it depends on the resource and its effects on the community.

n13440ae4127.s: Article 37 declares the Directive Principles to be:
o: Enforceable only during a national emergency
Fundamental in the governance of the country
n13440ae4127.x: Article 37 makes them non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country, and the State must apply them in making laws.

n9b4c4de4683.s: If Fundamental Rights are the means, the Directive Principles are described as the:
n9b4c4de4683.x: Fundamental Rights provide the means through which the social and economic goals (ends) of the Directive Principles are pursued.

nindian-polity-17-7.x: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable obligations of citizens only; being available against the State describes Fundamental Rights.

n560e1da5e8b.s: How many Fundamental Duties did the Swaran Singh Committee suggest?
n560e1da5e8b.x: The Committee suggested eight duties; the 42nd Amendment (1976) added ten.

nb1f01804005.s: The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 relates to the Fundamental Duty to:
o: Promote harmony and prevent caste or religious offences
Respect the National Flag and National Anthem
Protect the sovereignty and integrity of India
nb1f01804005.x: The UAPA, 1967 is linked to the duty under Article 51A(c); the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 relates to harmony.

nindian-polity-17-15.s: Under Article 51A(g), the natural environment that citizens must protect includes:
o: Monuments and places of national importance
nindian-polity-17-15.x: Article 51A(g) covers forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife and compassion for living creatures; it is not limited to forests and rivers.

nfe86a54e034.s: The Swaran Singh Committee proposal, not accepted, was that penalties for non-compliance with duties be prescribed by:
nfe86a54e034.x: The Committee proposed that Parliament could prescribe penalties for non-compliance; this was not accepted.

n1a4ba3ce922.s: The Swaran Singh Committee's proposal of payment of taxes as a Fundamental Duty was:
n1a4ba3ce922.x: Payment of taxes was suggested by the Committee but not accepted; 51A(i) is safeguarding public property and 51A(j) is excellence.

n8a784ea0770.s: Protection of monuments of national importance is provided under:
n8a784ea0770.x: Protection of monuments is Article 49, a Directive Principle; 51A(h) covers scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry.

ne3b6fb3d1cb.s: Fundamental Duties may be given legal effect through:
o: Writs of constitutional courts without any law
ne3b6fb3d1cb.x: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, but legislation may enforce them and courts may refer to them in interpretation.

nfe3fcd8d9a7.s: Which case held that Fundamental Duties cannot override Fundamental Rights and that respect for national symbols needs no compelled participation?
o: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala
nfe3fcd8d9a7.x: In Bijoe Emmanuel (1986), the Court held Fundamental Duties cannot override Part III rights.

nd2646ae6183.s: Courts may consider Fundamental Duties in assessing the ____ of a law restricting a Fundamental Right.
nd2646ae6183.x: Courts use Fundamental Duties as an aid in judging the reasonableness of restrictions, though duties cannot override Fundamental Rights.

ne1b8cae1202.s: Which of the following is a recognised significance of the Fundamental Duties?
o: They provide a basis for suspending all Fundamental Rights
They can be enforced through writs
They help courts assess the reasonableness of laws
They override Fundamental Rights in a conflict
ne1b8cae1202.x: Fundamental Duties help courts judge the reasonableness of laws; they do not justify suspending Fundamental Rights.

n151f9f4747b.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Fundamental Duty – Automatically overrides a Fundamental Right
n151f9f4747b.x: Articles 25 and 26 relate to freedom of religion, which Fundamental Duties cannot curtail; Article 48A is a Directive Principle, a duty of the State.

n916cd9ba1da.s: Critics say the Fundamental Duties are not exhaustive because they omit:
n916cd9ba1da.x: The list omits duties such as voting, paying taxes and family planning; the others are already covered.

new.s: Article 43B on co-operative societies was added by which Amendment?
new.x: The 97th Amendment, 2011 added Article 43B, the last DPSP added.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about amendments to the Directive Principles:
1. The 44th Amendment added Article 38(2).
2. The 86th Amendment substituted Article 45.
3. The 42nd Amendment added Article 44.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 44th added 38(2) and the 86th substituted Article 45; the UCC (Article 44) was not added by the 42nd Amendment.

new.s: Article 39A on free legal aid came into force on:
new.x: Article 39A was added in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment and came into force on 3 January 1977; 9 November 1995 is when the Legal Services Authorities Act came into force.

new.s: Ireland had itself borrowed the idea of Directive Principles from the Constitution of:
new.x: India borrowed the DPSPs from the Irish Constitution of 1937, which had copied the idea from Spain.

new.s: Which body split rights into justiciable and non-justiciable categories?
new.x: The Sapru Committee (1945) divided rights into justiciable and non-justiciable ones, an antecedent of Part IV.

new.s: Instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage is directed by Article:
new.x: Article 350A, outside Part IV, directs mother-tongue instruction; 350B provides a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

new.s: Article 335, a directive outside Part IV, concerns:
o: Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage
Claims of SCs and STs to services
new.x: Article 335 deals with claims of SCs and STs to services, consistent with efficiency of administration; Hindi is Article 351.

new.s: Which State was the first to adopt a State Uniform Civil Code?
new.x: Uttarakhand was the first State with a UCC and Gujarat the second; Goa follows the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867.

new.s: Article 43B (co-operative societies) falls under which group of Directive Principles?
new.x: Article 43B is a Gandhian principle; Articles 38, 39A and 47 are in the Socialistic group.

new.s: How many Articles are counted in the Gandhian group of Directive Principles?
new.x: The Gandhian group has six Articles: 40, 43, 43B, 46, 47 and 48.

new.s: Article 43A provides for workers' participation in the management of:
new.x: Article 43A, added by the 42nd Amendment, concerns workers' participation in the management of industries, not agriculture.

new.s: Who called the Directive Principles a 'novel feature' of the Constitution?
new.x: Ambedkar's 'novel feature' is the only approving remark; K.C. Wheare called them a manifesto of aims and aspirations.

new.s: Who described the Directive Principles as 'pious aspirations'?
new.x: Ivor Jennings called them pious aspirations; K.T. Shah compared them to a cheque payable at the bank's convenience.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a Directive Principle of State Policy?
new.x: The Right to Information is a legal right under the RTI Act, 2005; right to work (41), UCC (44) and maternity relief (42) are DPSPs.

new.s: The National Social Assistance Programme, which meets the directive of Article 41, was launched on:
new.x: The NSAP was launched on 15 August 1995 and serves the directives on right to work, education and public assistance (Article 41).

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Fundamental Rights – Moral and political sanction
new.x: Fundamental Rights aim at political democracy and carry legal sanction; DPSPs are non-justiciable with moral and political sanction.

new.s: Which clause of Article 39 directs that the tender age of children and the health of workers are not abused?
new.x: Article 39(e) protects the health and strength of workers and the tender age of children; 39(d) is equal pay for equal work.

new.s: How many Articles does Part IV (Articles 36-51) contain?
new.x: Part IV runs from Article 36 to Article 51, i.e. 16 articles.

new.s: Article 15(4), the response to Champakam Dorairajan, overcame the bar applied in that case under Article:
new.x: Champakam struck down a communal order under Article 29(2); the 1st Amendment inserted Article 15(4) in response.

new.s: Article 15(4) enables special provisions for:
o: Socially and educationally backward classes, SCs and STs
new.x: Article 15(4), inserted by the 1st Amendment, 1951, provides for socially and educationally backward classes, SCs and STs.

new.s: Reading Article 45 with Article 21 led to Article 21A through which Amendment?
new.x: DPSPs strengthened FRs: Article 45 read with 21 led to Article 21A by the 86th Amendment, 2002.

new.s: In which case was the balance between Parts III and IV held to be part of the Basic Structure?
new.x: Minerva Mills (1980) held the FR-DPSP balance to be part of the Basic Structure; absolute primacy to either destroys it.

new.s: The Twenty-fifth Amendment, 1971 was a response to which case?
new.x: The 25th Amendment answered R.C. Cooper (1970), replacing 'compensation' with 'amount' and inserting Article 31C.

new.s: Privy purses were abolished by which Amendment?
new.x: The 26th Amendment, 1971, responding to the Privy Purses case, abolished privy purses.

new.s: Which Amendment widened the meaning of 'estate' in Article 31A?
new.x: The 17th Amendment, 1964 widened 'estate' and allowed acquisition of land under personal cultivation only at market value.

new.s: Which Amendment made the adequacy of compensation non-justiciable?
new.x: The 4th Amendment, 1955 made adequacy of compensation non-justiciable.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Twenty-fourth Amendment, 1971:
1. It was a response to Golaknath.
2. It made the President's assent to Constitution Amendment Bills mandatory.
3. It inserted Article 31C.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 24th answered Golaknath and made the President's assent mandatory; Article 31C was inserted by the 25th Amendment.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles?
o: A law violating a Fundamental Right is void under Article 13
Directive Principles aim at social and economic democracy
The 44th Amendment gave Directive Principles primacy over Articles 14 and 19
Parliament may amend Fundamental Rights to implement Directive Principles within the basic structure
new.x: The attempt to give all DPSPs primacy over Articles 14 and 19 was the 42nd Amendment, struck down in Minerva Mills, not the 44th.

new.s: How many judges heard the Kesavananda Bharati case?
new.x: Kesavananda had a 13-judge bench, the largest; Golaknath had 11.

new.s: Sanjeev Coke (1983) held that Article 39(b) includes:
o: Only resources owned by the Union
Only natural resources owned by States
new.x: Sanjeev Coke (1983) held that 39(b) includes privately owned resources, following Krishna Iyer's view.

new.s: Besides striking down the 42nd Amendment's extension of Article 31C, Minerva Mills held that a proclamation of Emergency is:
new.x: Minerva Mills (1980) also held that an Emergency proclamation is subject to judicial review.

new.s: In I.R. Coelho (2007), the 'golden triangle' test for Ninth Schedule laws refers to Articles:
new.x: I.R. Coelho held there is no blanket immunity; laws are tested against the Basic Structure and Articles 14, 19 and 21.

new.s: In Ranganatha Reddy (1977), the minority view that 39(b) includes all privately owned resources was given by:
new.x: Krishna Iyer's minority view in Ranganatha Reddy was rejected in Property Owners Association (2024), written by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud.

new.s: Property Owners Association v. State of Maharashtra (2024) was decided by a Bench of how many judges?
new.x: A 9-judge Bench decided it by a 7:2 majority on 5 November 2024.

new.s: Which of the following cases was decided after Minerva Mills (1980)?
new.x: Sanjeev Coke came in 1983, after Minerva Mills; the others are earlier (1951, 1967, 1973).

new.s: Which of the following Parts was, like Part IVA, added to the Constitution after 1950?
new.x: The four Parts added after 1950 are IVA, IXA, IXB and XIVA; Part VI deals with the States.

new.s: The 42nd Amendment, which inserted the Fundamental Duties, came into force on:
new.x: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 came into force on 3 January 1977.

new.s: How many members did the Swaran Singh Committee have?
new.x: The Swaran Singh Committee had 12 members; it suggested 8 duties.

new.s: The need for the Swaran Singh Committee was felt during the:
new.x: The Committee was set up by the Congress party in 1976 during the Internal Emergency of 1975–77, not 1962.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the applicability of Fundamental Duties?
o: Article 51A(k) is addressed to parents or guardians
Article 51A(i) also applies to resident foreigners
Unlike Articles 14, 20, 21 and 25, they are not open to non-citizens
new.x: Fundamental Duties apply only to citizens; the statement that 51A(i) binds resident foreigners is false.

new.s: Which clause of Article 51A is classified as a moral duty?
new.x: The moral duties are (b), (f), (h) and (j); (a), (c) and (i) are civic duties.

new.s: Safeguarding public property is a Fundamental Duty under:
new.x: Article 51A(i) asks citizens to safeguard public property and abjure violence; 48A is a DPSP on the environment.

new.s: The J.S. Verma Committee linked the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 to the duty under Article:
new.x: The Protection of Civil Rights Act serves 51A(e) – harmony and no caste or religion offences.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Fundamental Duties – Addressed to the State
new.x: Fundamental Duties are in Part IVA (Article 51A) and are addressed to citizens; DPSPs are Articles 36–51.

new.s: Which jurist described others holding back from interfering with a right as a duty?
new.x: Holland explained that others holding back from interfering is called a duty, reflecting that rights and duties are correlative.

new.s: Under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, CSR spending must be at least what share of average net profit?
new.x: CSR is at least 2% of average net profit; the SC (Mar 2026) held corporations also carry the 51A(g) duty.

new.s: In the Preamble, the look-alike of the Fundamental Duty of common brotherhood under Article 51A(e) is:
new.x: The duty of common brotherhood (51A(e)) mirrors Fraternity in the Preamble.

new.s: Which of the following appears only as a Fundamental Duty, with no look-alike in the DPSPs?
new.x: Scientific temper (51A(h)) is only a Fundamental Duty; environment (48A), heritage (49) and education (45) have DPSP look-alikes.

new.s: Which case recognised a clean environment as part of Article 21?
new.x: Subhash Kumar (1991) read a clean environment into Article 21.

new.s: Critics object to the placement of Fundamental Duties because they are:
o: An appendage to Part IV instead of following Part III
new.x: Critics say placing them as an appendage to Part IV, not after Part III, reduces their value.

new.s: The 42nd Amendment moved forests and protection of wild animals and birds to the Concurrent List as Entries:
new.x: Along with 51A(g) and 48A, the 42nd Amendment created Entries 17A and 17B in the Concurrent List.

new.s: Protecting the weaker sections from social injustice is a directive under:
new.x: It is not a Fundamental Duty; it is DPSP Article 46.
